archetype.name: Pocket Passer (late-career, short-area)
archetype.definition: A 43-year-old who wins from the pocket with timing throws between the numbers and to his tight ends. He rarely moves, rarely scrambles, and no longer completes the deep ball often.

report.headline: Volume and touchdowns hide a below-average passer; Pittsburgh's run game should lead.
report.take:
Rodgers' surface line looks like a useful starter: 223.8 passing yards a game (18th of 54) and a 28-touchdown pace for a winning team. The efficiency underneath is below average. He sits at -0.051 EPA per dropback (34th), a -2.86 CPOE (38th) and 6.35 yards per attempt (36th), all under the qualifier average. His career line shows the same thing from another angle. From 2022 through 2025 he settled in as a mid-pack passer ranked in the high 20s to 30 by EPA, and this season he has slid a little further. His completion rate is down 5.8 points and his CPOE 2.9 points from last year.

The passing game splits sharply by area. Between the numbers he is still very good: 0.407 EPA on 67 throws to the middle, 0.243 EPA on intermediate attempts, and a +4 CPOE on short throws. His tight ends get the most from him. Pat Freiermuth (0.297 EPA per target) and Darnell Washington (0.189) both beat DK Metcalf, who draws far more volume at 0.071. Outside the hashes, behind the line and deep, the numbers fall apart. He completes 20.5% of throws of 20-plus air yards with a -14.8 CPOE, and screens and swings behind the line have cost 9.9 EPA in total.

The drives die on sacks, not interceptions. His line keeps him clean: he is pressured on only 18.2% of dropbacks, ninth-lowest. But 37.1% of those pressures become sacks (31st of 42), and on third down he has taken 17 sacks while converting just 29.9% at an average of 7.6 yards to go. That is not the cost of a scrambler hunting for big plays. He has four scrambles all year and a 2.75-second time to throw, up from 2.59. Taking sacks under pressure has been his profile for years: 34.1% pressure-to-sack last season, 31.5% in Jets green before that. At 43 it is who he is.

The odd part is the play-calling. Pittsburgh owns the league's best rushing EPA, yet passes 3.1 points more than situations call for (third-most) with the 26th-ranked pass offense. The last three games hint at a correction. He averaged 28 attempts and 175.7 yards in that stretch, while his EPA per dropback improved to 0.024. Fewer, cleaner throws is the version of Rodgers that helps this team. It is also a version with a lower fantasy ceiling.

strengths.title: Timing throws between the numbers
strengths.body: His best football is anticipatory throws to the middle and intermediate zones, where his accuracy and processing still show up. Those areas carry nearly all of his positive passing value. This is the most durable part of his game, because it relies on timing rather than arm or legs.

strengths.title: Tight ends are his best reads
strengths.body: Freiermuth and Washington produce far more per target than either outside receiver. That fits a passer who works the seams and the middle. Two big tight ends on the field also pair naturally with the league's best run game. Expect this to hold while both stay healthy.

strengths.title: Clean pockets, careful ball
strengths.body: His line limits how often he is pressured, and his interception rate sits under the league average. His bad-throw rate also dropped from last year. The protection part is now at risk: starting guard Mason McCormick is doubtful after a significant ankle injury.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: When pressure does arrive, he goes down far more often than most. The sacks pile up on third down and in the red zone, the two places drives are decided. It is a long-standing trait, not a slump. He no longer escapes, and his time to throw has crept up. Losing McCormick could make it worse.

concerns.title: The deep ball is mostly gone
concerns.body: He completes about one in five throws of 20-plus air yards, with a CPOE nearly 15 points below expected. Four touchdowns against three interceptions keep it roughly break-even. His aggressiveness into tight windows is up from last year, which makes these low-percentage shots a choice, not a necessity.

concerns.title: Passing more than the offense warrants
concerns.body: Pittsburgh ranks first in rushing EPA but 26th in passing EPA, yet it throws well above expectation in neutral situations. That inflates his volume and his negative EPA alike. If the staff leans into the run, his efficiency should improve while his yardage shrinks, as it has over the last three games.

trend.note: Early weeks swung wildly, from -16.8 EPA at New England to +6.7 against Cincinnati. Since the Week 7 trip to New Orleans his per-dropback efficiency has hovered just above average while attempts, yards and completion rate have slid. He also played only 82% of snaps in the Week 10 blowout loss.

nextGame.headline: Soft Eagles pass rush suits him, but the script favors the run
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia is close to the ideal opponent for his weakness. Its defense ranks 31st in QB hit rate and 27th in sack rate, so the pressure that turns into sacks against him should be scarce. It also ranks 26th in pass EPA allowed and gives up 18.5 PPR points a game to quarterbacks (24th). The catch is the game script. Pittsburgh is a 4.5-point favorite with a 38.5 total against an offense ranked 29th in EPA, and the Eagles are 30th against the run. That points to plenty of carries and a modest throw count. Philadelphia funnels targets to wide receivers (67.4% vs a 58% league share) and has held top tight ends under their norms, which cuts against his best reads. The forecast is early, but gusts near 29 mph with rain showers would further squeeze a deep game that is already broken.

On his side, McCormick's doubtful status removes a 93%-snap guard, which matters for a passer who rarely escapes. McCarthy is hopeful Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson return from IR. Either would give him a more reliable outside option than Germie Bernard, whose targets have been below average. For Philadelphia, both cornerbacks listed out, Michael Carter II and Jonathan Jones, are depth players. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell (out) and Zack Baun (questionable) were regulars in the middle of the field, where Rodgers does his best work. Those reports date from early November, so check final statuses.

keyMatchups.title: Weak rush versus his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: The Eagles rarely hit or sack quarterbacks, which reduces the drive-killing negatives that define his season. Without McCormick, though, his interior protection is thinner. A clean pocket is the single biggest lever on his efficiency.

keyMatchups.title: Metcalf against a soft WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia allows 0.42 EPA per target to opposing WR1s, 25th in the league, and pushes targets to receivers. That is a chance to get more from Metcalf, whose 70 targets have produced only modest value.

keyMatchups.title: Run game likely carries the day
keyMatchups.body: The league's best rushing offense faces the 30th-ranked run defense as a road favorite in a low-total game. That likely means fewer dropbacks for Rodgers and a lower yardage ceiling.

nextGame.watch: Who replaces McCormick at guard, and whether Rodgers' third-down sacks stay down against a pass rush that rarely gets home.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect roughly what the last three games showed: a capable short-and-middle passer on a run-first winner, with yardage drifting toward 190-230 a game instead of the early-season peaks. His third-down and red-zone sacks are a years-long trait and won't disappear. A 1.9% interception rate on a deep game this inaccurate may tick up. The returns of Pittman and Wilson are his best path to more efficiency, because they give him outside answers he hasn't had since Week 4.

Touchdowns have been the steadying force: 15 in nine games, and 9 in the red zone despite poor red-zone EPA. That rate leans on volume and on the tight ends near the goal line. If Pittsburgh keeps leaning on its run game, look for roughly 1 to 1.7 touchdowns a game, which leaves him a low-end starter in fantasy rather than a weekly difference-maker.
swingFactors: Pittman and Wilson returning from IR
How far McCarthy leans on the top-ranked run game

confidence.note: Nine starts plus a long career baseline make his profile clear; receiver returns and the guard injury add uncertainty.
